sources.notes: Declared demand, efficiency, PUE, and fictional tariff assumptions; no measured facility data
1,000 kW × 8,760 h × assumed PUE (1.25 or 1.15); tariff USD 0.10/kWh. Original mathematical examples, not a market quote or equipment validation.

The original 1 MW fixture is scaled by 50 in electrical demand, capacities and storage: 50 MW requested IT power, 5 MWh stored battery energy, 30-second generator delay and unchanged efficiencies/event times. An aggregate electrical load example, not measured GPU jobs, a server count, grid adequacy, equipment selection or a facility prediction.

One-variable teaching exercises in power, energy, losses, finite storage, generator timing, path capacity, common failures, recovery and separate assumed-PUE annual energy. Worked answers apply to the stated default and challenge inputs. Path capacity is only one N+1 condition. PUE does not model cooling or supply continuity. No independent external review is claimed.

The original 1 MW fixture is scaled by 200 in electrical demand, asset capacities and storage. Nominal aggregate IT demand is 200 MW; the outage case starts with 20 MWh stored energy. Efficiencies and generator delay are unchanged. An original teaching assumption, not an industry average, measured workload, selected equipment or calibrated facility. Profile names do not introduce workload behavior.

The original 1 MW fixture is scaled by 5 in electrical demand, asset capacities and storage. Nominal aggregate IT demand is 5 MW; the outage case starts with 0.5 MWh stored energy. Efficiencies and generator delay are unchanged. An original teaching assumption, not an industry average, measured workload, selected equipment or calibrated facility. Profile names do not introduce workload behavior.

Four profiles use nominal IT loads of 50, 200, 30 and 5 MW. Load-step cases change demand to 80%, 110% and 100% at 300, 600 and 900 seconds. Extended-reserve cases replace the baseline storage with four hours of gross initial energy, disable charging, run four hours and remove utility/generator supply from 300 to 11100 seconds. Added outage cases retain the baseline event schedule. Overrides are explicit synthetic inputs, not GPU transients, renewable dispatch, grid-forming controls, black start or equipment response. Energy coverage does not establish uptime.
